findings.title: Unsubscribe GET is not idempotent and does not stop topic emails
findings.body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe changes notification_level on every request: tracking/watching (above regular) is set to regular, and regular or muted is set to muted. A watching user — the usual case for topic notification mail, including category auto-watch — is only dropped to regular, so reply, mention, quote, and category-watch emails continue, despite the email and page copy saying notifications for that topic will stop. Because the same transition runs again on refresh, prefetch, or a second click, that user is then muted. The action is also not safe to retry: there is no confirmation step and no check that the level was already updated.

findings.title: Missing TopicUser crashes unsubscribe and the change is not recorded
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil (user never had a topic_users row, or it was removed). The next line calls tu.notification_level and raises NoMethodError, so the unsubscribe link 500s instead of muting the topic. When a row does exist, tu.save! writes notification_level directly and skips TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at stay unset and no MessageBus notification_level_change is published. update_last_read auto-promotes to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and view time exceeds the auto-track threshold, which silently undoes the unsubscribe on a later visit. Other open tabs also keep the old level.

findings.title: Topic unsubscribe is a cookie-authenticated GET with no recipient token
findings.body: Both unsubscribe routes are GET and TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification state with no CSRF token and no per-recipient key (unlike digest unsubscribe). Rails does not check authenticity tokens on GET, so a logged-in user's browser will apply the change for any third-party page that can trigger the URL (img, redirect, or link prefetch). The link is also not bound to the email recipient: whoever is logged in is the account that is changed, and a logged-out recipient is not unsubscribed until after a login round-trip.

findings.title: Unsubscribe template will not resolve for the new route
findings.body: The route is registered as a top-level topicUnsubscribe (/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe), and the route, controller, and view files are all named topic-unsubscribe, so Ember looks up the template topic-unsubscribe. This file is registered as topic/unsubscribe (the nested topic.unsubscribe name). Nothing sets templateName or renderTemplate, so the confirmation copy and the topic-notifications-button never render. After the Rails action mutates notification level, the user gets a missing-template error instead of the unsubscribe page. The Ember route also never calls an unsubscribe API itself, so a client-side transition to this URL would show the "you will stop receiving notifications" text without changing the level even if the template name were fixed.

findings.title: No tests for per-topic unsubscribe behavior
findings.body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into Email::MessageBuilder so the new %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation does not raise. Nothing asserts that the topic link is actually rendered, and there is no request/controller coverage for unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted transitions, a second request not changing the level again, slug redirect, or the login/CSRF constraints. The level rules are easy to get wrong and would regress silently.
